Compile MIR text to an R function

Source: R/mir_function.R
mir_function.Rd

mir_function() reads a module in MIR's textual form, compiles the function name from it on tier, and returns an R function that calls the result. It is for tests, teaching, and checking a code generator's output by hand; MIR's text format is described in MIR's MIR.md.

Usage

mir_function(text, name, tier = NULL)

Arguments

text

MIR text: one string with one or more modules.

name

The name of the function to call.

tier

"native" or "interp"; by default zumir_tier().

Value

A function of class zumir_function. Its context lives as long as the function does.

Details

The function must be exported by its module (export name), and take and return numbers only: the integer types i8 to u64, f and d, with at most one result. The R function has one argument per MIR argument, by the same names, each a single number. An integer argument must be a whole number that fits its type. Results of 8 to 32 bits are R integers; 64-bit results and u32 are doubles, and one beyond 2^53 is an error, since a double could not hold it exactly.

The code may call the C math library and memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen by name (import exp); any other import is a link error. Compiled code runs with the rights of .Call() code: a wrong memory access crashes R, as it would in a package's C code.

See also

Other compilers: rfunction()

Examples

add <- mir_function("
  m: module
     export add
  add: func d, d:a, d:b
     local d:r
     dadd r, a, b
     ret r
     endfunc
     endmodule", "add")
add(1, 2)
#> [1] 3
